thread:
mike: quick heads-up — ran nightly perf suite against Llama3-13B variations and saw a 12-18% p99 latency bump when kernel selector flips to the small-head fused path
anya: ugh, that's the path that uses the blocked matmul kernel right? any repro notes?
mike: yeah, seems tied to head_dim=64 / hidden=8192 combos. profiler shows matmul/transpose path switching. flame shows matmul_spmm_smallHeads taking most time
kevin: can you paste the profiler snippet (ops + time %) so we can see where warmups are happening?
mike: putting a short extract: 
```
op: attention_kernel_matmul_small_heads   time: 46.3%   calls: 1200
op: transpose_heads_fused                 time: 18.9%   calls: 1200
op: kv_cache_eviction_check               time: 6.2%    calls: 1200
op: fallback_padding_copy                 time: 5.5%    calls: 1200
others                                     time: 23.1%
```
anya: KV eviction check at 6% seems high — are we seeing more stride updates or frequent cache invalidations?
mike: not invalidations exactly. The runtime is hitting a slower path because RoPE theta scaling in model config triggers a sequence-length dependent kernel choice; for certain chat templates (short prompt + many turns) the selector underestimates prefix reuse and we lose KV cache locality
sarah: that matches the request histogram I saw — lots of 64->512 seq-length oscillation. selector heuristics assume monotonic growth which isn't true for chat-turn workloads
kevin: can you share the quick repro shell command? I can run a microbenchmark with specific head/hidden combos and baseline kernels
mike: sure: 
```
# repro: run perf micro with head_dim=64 hidden_size=8192
python tools/perf_micro.py --model llama3-13b --head-dim 64 --hidden-size 8192 --rope-theta auto --profile --seqs 64,256,64 --batch 8
```
kevin: running now. also toggling `--rope-theta 1.0` vs `auto` to see if explicit override avoids selector swap
perf-bot: benchmark queued: job id 9773 (llama3-13b head64 hidden8192 seqs 64,256,64) — ETA ~8m
anya: if kernel selector is using rope_theta-derived heuristics, we should decouple kernel choice from RoPE config. RoPE affects attention indexing but shouldn't force a matmul kernel swap for identical memory shapes
mike: Agreed. Hypothesis: we have a rule: if rope_theta < threshold => prefer fused_small_heads kernel (better numerical stability). But for certain head/hidden shapes that's slower on A100 due to launch overheads
sarah: Also check SiLU/RMSNorm combos. Llama3 uses RMSNorm+SiLU fused op which can change kernel fusion opportunities and push matmul into different scheduling bins
kevin: Result from local run: p99 increased by 15% with `--rope-theta auto`. With `--rope-theta 1.0` it drops back to baseline. Breakdown: small_heads kernel 47% vs fused_large 22%
mike: solid repro. Next steps: 1) add deterministic override to kernel selector for head_dim/hidden pairs we know are slow 2) decouple rope_theta influence from kernel binning 3) add a microbenchmark test that runs the chat-turn seq oscillation pattern
anya: I'll open an RFC/issue and sketch selector rules. Suggest adding a cost-model parameter: predicted_launch_overhead + runtime_bandwidth_estimate => choose kernel. Keep rope_theta only for numerical-path decisions not perf bins
kevin: I'll prototype a quick cost-estimator in selector that samples both kernels for a representative batch and caches the decision per model+shape combo
mike: timestamped perf logs saved under s3://redwood-perf/llama3/2168800123/ — contains full trace and the sample workloads
perf-bot: issue created: #4761 kernel-selector: decouple RoPE heuristics from perf bins (link: https://redwood.internal/issue/4761)
sarah: assigning to kevin + anya for initial patch, mike for validation. Can we get this into next week's runtime canary?
kevin: yes, prototype by EOD tomorrow, canary early next week if tests pass
anya: will add microbench to ci/perf and a quick eval to ensure no accuracy regressions with different kernel choices
mike: thanks team — this explains the regression and gives an actionable path. ping me if you need kernel-level profiling knobs
kevin: noted. starting now.
